∀ {n : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq n] [inst_1 : Fintype n] {R : Type v} [inst_2 : CommRing R] {S : Type w}
  [inst_3 : CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) (M : Matrix n n R), f M.det = (f.mapMatrix M).det
items.informal_description: For any ring homomorphism $ f : R \to S $ between commutative rings and any $ n \times n $ matrix $ M $ with entries in $ R $, the determinant of the matrix obtained by applying $ f $ to each entry of $ M $ is equal to $ f $ applied to the determinant of $ M $. Formally, $ \det(f_{\ast}(M)) = f(\det(M)) $, where $ f_{\ast}(M) $ denotes the matrix with entries $ f(M_{ij}) $.

  [inst_3 : CommRing S] (f : R ≃+* S) (M : Matrix n n R), f M.det = (f.mapMatrix M).det
items.informal_description: For any ring isomorphism $ f : R \to S $ between commutative rings and any square matrix $ M $ with entries in $ R $, the determinant of the matrix obtained by applying $ f $ to each entry of $ M $ is equal to the image of the determinant of $ M $ under $ f $. Symbolically, $ \det(f_*M) = f(\det M) $, where $ f_*M $ denotes the matrix with entries transformed by $ f $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Determinant with Algebra Homomorphisms
items.informal_description: For any commutative ring $ R $, $ R $-algebras $ S $ and $ T $, finite type $ n $, algebra homomorphism $ f : S \to T $, and square matrix $ M \in \text{Mat}_{n \times n}(S) $, the determinant commutes with the algebra homomorphism: $ f(\det(M)) = \det(f_{*}(M)) $, where $ f_{*}(M) $ denotes the matrix obtained by applying $ f $ to each entry of $ M $. This equality holds due to the compatibility of determinants with scalar extensions and the multilinearity of the determinant function.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {n : Type u_4} {m : Type u_5} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S]
  (M : Matrix m m S) [inst_2 : DecidableEq m] [inst_3 : DecidableEq n] [inst_4 : Fintype m] [inst_5 : Fintype n]
  (f : S →+* Matrix n n R), (f M.det).det = ((Matrix.comp m m n n R) (M.map ⇑f)).det
items.informal_description: For finite types $ m $ and $ n $, and a ring homomorphism $ f : S 	o 	ext{Matrix } n n R $, the determinant of $ f $ applied to the determinant of a matrix $ M $ equals the determinant of the composed matrix obtained by applying $ f $ to each entry of $ M $ and then flattening the resulting matrix of matrices into a larger matrix via the canonical equivalence.

For any ring homomorphism $f : R \to S$ and any invertible $n \times n$ matrix $g$ over $R$, the determinant of the matrix obtained by applying $f$ to each entry of $g$ is equal to the result of applying $f$ to the determinant of $g$. In symbols, $\det(f(g)) = f(\det(g))$.
